exposure: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings (including Diffusion Weighted Imaging (DWI))
cohort: A total of 81 neonates diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) who underwent therapeutic hypothermia.
finding: Diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) was found to be superior to cranial ultrasound (cUS) in determining the severity of hypoxic injury, and renal involvement was associated with poor neurodevelopmental outcomes.
followup_time: MRI performed within the first 7 days of life; follow-up duration for neurodevelopmental outcomes not specified.
